publication_boundary: Private owner-review material. No legal record in this file is automatically included in either public product.

records.case_name: First Nations Child and Family Caring Society of Canada et al. v. Attorney General of Canada
records.anonymized_title: Tribunal found discriminatory federal First Nations child-and-family service funding and Jordan's Principle implementation
allegations: The federal First Nations child-and-family services funding model and narrow implementation of Jordan's Principle denied equal services to First Nations children and families.
findings: The Tribunal substantiated the complaint and found discrimination contrary to section 5 of the Canadian Human Rights Act.
records.remedy_or_outcome: The Tribunal ordered Canada to cease the discriminatory practices, reform the program and implement the full meaning and scope of Jordan's Principle; later compliance and compensation orders remain a separate evidence chain.
records.healthcare_relevance: Jordan's Principle includes access to health, social and educational supports without jurisdictional delay.

records.case_name: Canada (Attorney General) v. First Nations Child and Family Caring Society of Canada
records.anonymized_title: Federal Court reviewed Tribunal compensation and Jordan's Principle eligibility orders
allegations: Canada challenged Canadian Human Rights Tribunal compensation and eligibility orders.
findings: The Federal Court dismissed the applications for judicial review, leaving the challenged Tribunal orders in place.
records.remedy_or_outcome: Applications dismissed; later settlement and implementation material must be tracked separately and is not proved by this judgment alone.
records.healthcare_relevance: The reviewed orders included Jordan's Principle eligibility and service access.

records.case_name: Canada (Attorney General) v. PHS Community Services Society
records.anonymized_title: Supreme Court required an exemption protecting continued operation of Insite
allegations: Refusal to continue a federal exemption threatened operation of a supervised injection facility and the health and safety of people who used it.
findings: The Court held that the Minister's refusal engaged section 7 and was arbitrary and grossly disproportionate on the record before it.
records.remedy_or_outcome: The Court ordered the Minister to grant an exemption to Insite under the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act.
records.healthcare_relevance: Supervised consumption, overdose response, counselling and health-service access.

records.case_name: Stewart v. Elk Valley Coal Corp.
records.anonymized_title: Supreme Court considered addiction, workplace policy and the required connection to adverse treatment
allegations: The termination was alleged to be discrimination based on drug dependence.
findings: The majority upheld the Tribunal's conclusion that the employee was terminated for breaching the policy and had not shown addiction was a factor in the adverse treatment on the record.
records.remedy_or_outcome: Appeal dismissed. The decision is a caution that addiction status and adverse treatment do not alone establish the required discriminatory connection.
records.healthcare_relevance: Addiction and disability law context rather than a treatment-access case.

records.case_name: Northern Regional Health Authority v. Horrocks
records.anonymized_title: Supreme Court resolved forum jurisdiction in a unionized employee's addiction-related human-rights dispute
allegations: The underlying dispute alleged discrimination related to alcohol addiction after termination from employment.
findings: The Supreme Court decision resolved exclusive arbitral jurisdiction; it was not a fresh merits determination of the discrimination allegation.
records.remedy_or_outcome: The human-rights adjudicator lacked jurisdiction because the dispute fell within the exclusive labour-arbitration regime.
records.healthcare_relevance: Employment by a health authority and addiction-disability context; not a patient-care case.

records.anonymized_title: Tribunal found race and disability discrimination in security treatment at a public mall
allegations: Security practices were alleged to discriminate against Indigenous and disabled people perceived as poor or homeless.
findings: The Tribunal found discrimination against the complainant in services based on race and disability and ordered individual and systemic remedies.
records.remedy_or_outcome: Individual compensation and systemic policy, training and implementation-related remedies were ordered.
records.healthcare_relevance: Not a healthcare case; relevant to security, homelessness, disability and Indigenous discrimination context.
records.accountable_organization: Henderson Development (Canada) Ltd. and Securiguard Services Ltd.

records.case_name: Mr. C v. Vancouver Coastal Health Authority
records.anonymized_title: Tribunal allowed an Indigenous healthcare discrimination complaint to proceed despite timing issues
allegations: The complaint alleged discrimination in healthcare connected to Indigenous identity and disability.
records.remedy_or_outcome: The Tribunal accepted the late-filed complaint as a procedural matter. It did not decide whether discrimination occurred.

records.case_name: Vancouver Area Network of Drug Users v. Downtown Vancouver Business Improvement Association
records.anonymized_title: Court of Appeal reviewed a representative discrimination complaint involving street homelessness and drug addiction
records.court_or_tribunal: Court of Appeal for British Columbia
allegations: A representative complaint alleged discriminatory treatment of people who were or appeared street homeless or drug addicted in public spaces.
findings: The Court of Appeal allowed the appeal and reinstated the Tribunal's dismissal of the complaint; the judgment did not establish the alleged discrimination.
records.remedy_or_outcome: Tribunal dismissal reinstated; the Supreme Court of Canada later dismissed leave to appeal.
records.healthcare_relevance: Not a healthcare case; relevant to homelessness, addiction, security and public-space discrimination law.
records.accountable_organization: Downtown Vancouver Business Improvement Association and City of Vancouver

records.anonymized_title: Tribunal found an employer failed to accommodate a worker's alcohol addiction
allegations: The complainant alleged disability discrimination after termination connected to conduct arising from alcohol addiction.
findings: The Tribunal found the employer knew or ought to have known about the addiction and failed to take steps to inquire or accommodate.
records.remedy_or_outcome: The Tribunal awarded injury-to-dignity damages, lost wages and benefits.
records.healthcare_relevance: Addiction treatment and disability accommodation context; not a healthcare-service case.

records.case_name: Ledger v. Alberta Health Services and Alberta Justice and Solicitor General
records.anonymized_title: Tribunal sent an Indigenous nurse's race-based workplace complaint to a full hearing
allegations: An Indigenous registered nurse alleged race-based threats, workplace abuse and inadequate institutional response after attending an anti-racism demonstration.
records.remedy_or_outcome: The dismissal was overturned and the complaint was sent to a full hearing; the matter later settled before hearing, so no public merits finding was made.
records.healthcare_relevance: Healthcare workforce and institutional response; not patient treatment.
records.accountable_organization: Alberta Health Services and Alberta Justice and Solicitor General
